Parcats traces

Source: R/zz-gen-figure.R, R/zz-gen-parcats.R
go_parcats.Rd

Parallel categories diagram for multidimensional categorical data.

Usage

add_parcats(fig, ...)

# Default S3 method
add_parcats(
  fig,
  ...,
  data = NULL,
  arrangement = NULL,
  bundlecolors = NULL,
  counts = NULL,
  dimensions = NULL,
  domain = NULL,
  hoverinfo = NULL,
  hoveron = NULL,
  hovertemplate = NULL,
  hovertemplatefallback = NULL,
  labelfont = NULL,
  legendgrouptitle = NULL,
  legendwidth = NULL,
  line = NULL,
  meta = NULL,
  name = NULL,
  sortpaths = NULL,
  tickfont = NULL,
  uid = NULL,
  uirevision = NULL,
  visible = NULL,
  row = NULL,
  col = NULL,
  skip_invalid = FALSE
)

go_parcats(
  ...,
  arrangement = NULL,
  bundlecolors = NULL,
  counts = NULL,
  dimensions = NULL,
  domain = NULL,
  hoverinfo = NULL,
  hoveron = NULL,
  hovertemplate = NULL,
  hovertemplatefallback = NULL,
  labelfont = NULL,
  legendgrouptitle = NULL,
  legendwidth = NULL,
  line = NULL,
  meta = NULL,
  name = NULL,
  sortpaths = NULL,
  tickfont = NULL,
  uid = NULL,
  uirevision = NULL,
  visible = NULL,
  skip_invalid = FALSE
)

Arguments

fig

A go_figure object.

...

Not for properties, which must be named in full: an abbreviated or unknown name is an error that suggests the right one.

data

A data frame in which formula properties (e.g. x = ~col, marker = list(size = ~col), marker = go_scatter_marker(size = ~col)) are evaluated. Default: the data given to go_figure(). Only the evaluated values are added to the trace. A crosstalk::SharedData works the same way, and links the trace to its crosstalk group (see highlight()).

arrangement

Sets the drag interaction mode for categories and dimensions. If `perpendicular`, the categories can only move along a line perpendicular to the paths. If `freeform`, the categories can freely move on the plane. If `fixed`, the categories and dimensions are stationary. One of "perpendicular", "freeform", "fixed".

bundlecolors

Sort paths so that like colors are bundled together within each category. Logical.

counts

The number of observations represented by each state. Defaults to 1 so that each state represents one observation Number in the interval [0, Inf], or a vector of these.

dimensions

List, each element a go_parcats_dimension() object or named list, with properties categoryarray, categoryorder, displayindex, label, ticktext, values and visible (see go_parcats_dimension()).

domain

A go_domain() object or named list, with properties column, row, x and y (see go_domain()).

hoverinfo

Determines what trace information appears on hover. If `none` or `skip` are set, no information is displayed upon hovering. But, if `none` is set, click and hover events are still fired. Any combination of "count", "probability" joined with "+", or one of "all", "none", "skip".

hoveron

Sets the hover interaction mode for the parcats diagram. If `category`, hover interaction take place per category. If `color`, hover interactions take place per color per category. If `dimension`, hover interactions take place across all categories per dimension. One of "category", "color", "dimension".

hovertemplate

Template string used for rendering the information that appear on hover box. Note that this will override `hoverinfo`. Variables are inserted using %{variable}, for example "y: %{y}" as well as %{xother}, {%_xother}, {%_xother_}, {%xother_}. When showing info for several points, "xother" will be added to those with different x positions from the first point. An underscore before or after "(x|y)other" will add a space on that side, only when this field is shown. Numbers are formatted using d3-format's syntax %{variable:d3-format}, for example "Price: %{y:$.2f}". https://github.com/d3/d3-format/tree/v1.4.5#d3-format for details on the formatting syntax. Dates are formatted using d3-time-format's syntax %{variable|d3-time-format}, for example "Day: %{2019-01-01|%A}". https://github.com/d3/d3-time-format/tree/v2.2.3#locale_format for details on the date formatting syntax. Variables that can't be found will be replaced with the specifier. For example, a template of "data: %{x}, %{y}" will result in a value of "data: 1, %{y}" if x is 1 and y is missing. Variables with an undefined value will be replaced with the fallback value. The variables available in `hovertemplate` are the ones emitted as event data described at this link https://plotly.com/javascript/plotlyjs-events/#event-data. Additionally, all attributes that can be specified per-point (the ones that are `arrayOk: true`) are available. Finally, the template string has access to variables `count`, `probability`, `category`, `categorycount`, `colorcount` and `bandcolorcount`. Anything contained in tag `<extra>` is displayed in the secondary box, for example `<extra>%{fullData.name}</extra>`. To hide the secondary box completely, use an empty tag `<extra></extra>`. String.

hovertemplatefallback

Fallback string that's displayed when a variable referenced in a template is missing. If the boolean value 'false' is passed in, the specifier with the missing variable will be displayed. Any value.

labelfont

Sets the font for the `dimension` labels. A go_font() object or named list, with properties color, family, lineposition, shadow, size, style, textcase, variant and weight (see go_font()).

legendgrouptitle

A go_legendgrouptitle() object or named list, with properties font and text (see go_legendgrouptitle()).

legendwidth

Sets the width (in px or fraction) of the legend for this trace. Number in the interval [0, Inf].

line

A go_parcats_line() object or named list, with properties autocolorscale, cauto, cmax, cmid, cmin, color, coloraxis, colorbar, colorscale, hovertemplate, hovertemplatefallback, reversescale, shape and showscale (see go_parcats_line()).

meta

Assigns extra meta information associated with this trace that can be used in various text attributes. Attributes such as trace `name`, graph, axis and colorbar `title.text`, annotation `text` `rangeselector`, `updatemenues` and `sliders` `label` text all support `meta`. To access the trace `meta` values in an attribute in the same trace, simply use `%{meta[i]}` where `i` is the index or key of the `meta` item in question. To access trace `meta` in layout attributes, use `%{data[n[.meta[i]}` where `i` is the index or key of the `meta` and `n` is the trace index. Any value.

name

Sets the trace name. The trace name appears as the legend item and on hover. String.

sortpaths

Sets the path sorting algorithm. If `forward`, sort paths based on dimension categories from left to right. If `backward`, sort paths based on dimensions categories from right to left. One of "forward", "backward".

tickfont

Sets the font for the `category` labels. A go_font() object or named list, with properties color, family, lineposition, shadow, size, style, textcase, variant and weight (see go_font()).

uid

Assign an id to this trace, Use this to provide object constancy between traces during animations and transitions. String.

uirevision

Controls persistence of some user-driven changes to the trace: `constraintrange` in `parcoords` traces, as well as some `editable: true` modifications such as `name` and `colorbar.title`. Defaults to `layout.uirevision`. Note that other user-driven trace attribute changes are controlled by `layout` attributes: `trace.visible` is controlled by `layout.legend.uirevision`, `selectedpoints` is controlled by `layout.selectionrevision`, and `colorbar.(x|y)` (accessible with `config: {editable: true}`) is controlled by `layout.editrevision`. Trace changes are tracked by `uid`, which only falls back on trace index if no `uid` is provided. So if your app can add/remove traces before the end of the `data` array, such that the same trace has a different index, you can still preserve user-driven changes if you give each trace a `uid` that stays with it as it moves. Any value.

visible

Determines whether or not this trace is visible. If "legendonly", the trace is not drawn, but can appear as a legend item (provided that the legend itself is visible). One of "legendonly", TRUE, FALSE.

row

Subplot grid row (figures created with make_subplots() only). May be "all" or a vector to address several cells.

col

Subplot grid column (figures created with make_subplots() only). May be "all" or a vector to address several cells.

skip_invalid

If TRUE, silently drop invalid properties instead of raising an error.

Value

go_*() functions return a graph object; add_*() functions return the modified figure.

Details

go_parcats() creates a validated graph object (a named list). add_parcats() creates one and adds it to a figure.

Nested objects are given as named lists or with their constructors, which are linked from the arguments below. Every property is checked against the plotly.js schema when the object is created or modified (see plotly_obj-modify). One-sided formulas (~col) are evaluated in the data, and then checked, when the trace is added with add_<trace>() or add_trace().

See also

go_figure(), add_trace()

Examples

mtcars |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_parcats(
    dimensions = list(
      go_parcats_dimension(label = "cyl", values = ~cyl),
      go_parcats_dimension(label = "gear", values = ~gear),
      go_parcats_dimension(label = "am", values = ~am)
    )
  )
